title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: id_exists() verifies whether identifiers exist respective registries. type = NULL, type inferred automatically: Return values: TRUE → confirmed registry FALSE → confirmed found NA → classified normalized
code: scholidonline::id_exists(   x    = "10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) ## [1] TRUE scholidonline::id_exists(   x = c(     "10.1000/182",     "12345678"   ) ) ## [1] TRUE TRUE

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: Many scholarly identifiers cross-linked across systems. Common examples: PMID → DOI PMCID → PMID DOI → PMCID = NULL, source type inferred per element: Unresolvable mappings return NA_character_.

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: id_metadata() retrieves harmonized metadata external registries. Returned metadata registry-derived minimally harmonized across providers. Typical columns include: input type provider title year container doi pmid pmcid url Metadata completeness depends external authority. can restrict returned fields:
code: scholidonline::id_metadata(   x    = "10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) ##         input type provider title year container  doi pmid pmcid  url ## 1 10.1000/182  doi     <NA>  <NA>   NA      <NA> <NA> <NA>  <NA> <NA> scholidonline::id_metadata(   x = "10.1000/182",   fields = c("title", "year", "doi") ) ##   title year  doi ## 1  <NA>   NA <NA>

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: id_links() returns related identifiers discovered via registry queries. may reveal: DOI PMID PMCID linked identifiers result long data.frame one row per link.
code: scholidonline::id_links(   x    = "PMC1234567",   type = "pmcid" ) ##        query query_type linked_type                        linked_id provider ## 1 PMC1234567      pmcid        pmid                          7717779     ncbi ## 3 PMC1234567      pmcid         doi 10.1097/00000658-199503000-00007     ncbi

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: common workflow messy identifier columns: Detect identifier types (via scholid) Normalize identifiers Check registry existence Convert enrich metadata Example: separation keeps structural logic (scholid) registry logic (scholidonline) clearly distinct.
code: x <- c(   "https://doi.org/10.1000/182",   "PMID: 12345678",   "not an id" )  types <- scholid::detect_scholid_type(x)  x_norm <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))  for (i in seq_along(x)) {   if (is.na(types[i])) {     next   }    x_norm[i] <- scholid::normalize_scholid(     x = x[i],     type = types[i]   ) }  types ## [1] "doi"  "issn" NA x_norm ## [1] "10.1000/182" "1234-5678"   NA scholidonline::id_exists(x) ## [1] TRUE   NA   NA

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: functions accept provider argument. provider = "auto" (default), sensible registry chosen automatically, potentially fallback behavior. Available providers depend identifier type operation. Use scholidonline_capabilities() inspect . chosen provider affects: Response speed Metadata richness Crosswalk coverage
code: scholidonline::id_exists(   x        = "10.1000/182",   type     = "doi",   provider = "crossref" ) ## [1] FALSE

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: vignette explains means validate scholarly identifiers external registries scholidonline relates scholid. working identifiers programmatically, essential distinguish three levels validity: Structural validity Checksum validity Registry validity scholid operates structural (, applicable, checksum) level. scholidonline operates registry level. fundamentally different layers.

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: Structural validity answers: string match formal grammar identifier system? Example: Structural validation uses regular expressions , applicable, checksum algorithms (e.g., ORCID). require internet access. confirm existence.
code: scholid::is_scholid(   "10.1000/182",   type = "doi"   ) ## [1] TRUE

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: Registry validity answers: identifier exist external authority? example: DOI resolve via doi.org Crossref? PMID exist PubMed? ORCID iD present ORCID registry? Example: Registry validation: Requires internet access Depends external APIs May affected rate limits temporary outages Can change time structurally valid identifier may still fail registry validation.
